lead.headline: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia's chief after Trump dials into its board meeting, as the US blacklists Megaspeed
lead.short: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, a day after Donald Trump dialled into its Sunday board meeting to argue for his return, Semafor reports. The same day, the US commerce department added Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia partner whose controlling shareholder is Alice Huang, to its trade blacklist. Nvidia's shares surged on the news.

why.text: The world's most important AI chipmaker is back under a chief forced out over national security fears, now with the president's backing.

more: Huang was forced to resign over a reported affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing; China calls the accusations "groundless". Trump also asked JD Vance to assure the board that Huang was not a security risk, the New York Times reports. Nvidia's chair had said Huang's behaviour was inconsistent with its code of conduct.

Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House oversight committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" raised "serious national security and corruption questions". Megaspeed, under US investigation since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, now needs approval for any US exports. Singapore's prime minister Lawrence Wong said his country is running its own inquiry.

update.new: Huang is reinstated and Megaspeed blacklisted.
update.front: Huang, who had been forced out, is now back in charge.

seconds.headline: Sheikh Hasina asks to fly home from Delhi on 16 December, and Dhaka says she can come back only in handcuffs
seconds.short: Sheikh Hasina, the deposed Bangladeshi prime minister living in India since August 2024, wants to return home on 16 December, Victory Day, her spokesperson told Reuters. On Tuesday Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, ruled out an unconditional return: "She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance."

why.text: Hasina has lived in Delhi for more than two years, and how she leaves will test India's ties with the government that replaced her.

more: Her spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said she wanted the Bangladesh government to arrange her flight from Delhi on the national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Victory Day marks the country's independence from Pakistan in 1971. Hasina fled to India in August 2024 after weeks of protests against her government, and has lived in Delhi since.

"A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," Kobir said after briefing foreign diplomats in Dhaka. "The reality is that no terrorist will ever be allowed to return this way without extradition," he added, according to The Daily Star, blaming what he called Awami terrorism sponsored by Hasina from Delhi.

facts.Dhaka's answer: only in handcuffs or under strict surveillance

seconds.headline: India pledges $1.62bn to rebuild Nepal after August's glacier floods, as Modi hosts Balendra Shah
seconds.short: India will give Nepal a $1.62bn development package after August's devastating floods, Narendra Modi announced on Monday after talks in New Delhi with Nepal's prime minister, Balendra Shah. It is one of India's largest-ever relief commitments, worth 240 billion Nepali rupees, and comes as New Delhi competes with China for influence in the Himalayan country.

why.text: The floods killed more than 1,300 people, and the package is India's biggest bid yet in its contest with China for sway in Nepal.

more: "To support Nepal's reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package," Modi said, standing beside Shah. It is Shah's first bilateral trip abroad since he came to power in March, and the visit lasts two days. New Delhi is stepping up ties with its Himalayan neighbour.

The floods began on 26 August when part of a mountain glacier collapsed and sent water and mud into Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions and China's Tibet. More than 5,000 people remain missing. Scientists blame climate change. In October the UN's climate loss and damage fund set aside $20m for Nepal.

update.front: The visit has now produced a $1.62bn package.

seconds.headline: Nato will defend against threats in space, Rutte says, after reports Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite within 60 days
seconds.short: Nato's secretary general Mark Rutte said the alliance will defend against any threats in space, after German media reported that Russia was preparing to launch a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead. Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days were shared among Nato countries this month. The Kremlin dismissed the reports as "hardly worth taking seriously".

why.text: A nuclear weapon in orbit could knock out the satellites that phones, banks and armies everywhere depend on.

more: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element," Rutte said at a press conference in Berlin with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. He said Nato had a variety of response options. "When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence," he added.

The reports, by broadcasters NDR and WDR and the newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, cite anonymous German military and intelligence sources. They say the satellite is called "Sputnik-S" and could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites. The Russian embassy in Berlin called them "unfounded allegations" and part of a "propaganda campaign".

stories.headline: The BJP and the Akali Dal reunite for the Punjab election, six years after splitting over the farm laws
stories.short: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal were set to announce their alliance for next year's Punjab assembly election at a joint press conference at the BJP's Delhi headquarters on Tuesday, with Amit Shah, BJP chief Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal attending. The Akalis walked out of the NDA in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.

why.text: Together they hope to win back Punjab from the Aam Aadmi Party, and the BJP wants a much bigger share of the seats this time.

more: Under their old arrangement the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 seats and the Akalis fought the rest. BJP sources say the party will now contest substantially more, as it campaigns against drug addiction and religious conversions by missionaries and brings in leaders from other parties. The party has been stepping up its outreach in the state for months.

The balance between the two has shifted. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election the BJP won more than 18% of the vote in Punjab and the Akali Dal just over 13%. The Akalis, once the dominant regional force, have been in decline since the Aam Aadmi Party swept the state.

stories.headline: Zelensky confirms Ukraine sank the Russian corvette in Benghazi, calling it "an exemplary operation"; Moscow calls it a dangerous escalation
stories.short: Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed that Ukraine carried out the night-time attack on the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya's Benghazi harbour, calling it "an exemplary operation". The strike was coordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, and Ukraine says it used naval drones. Russia has called it "a dangerous escalation".

why.text: Kyiv now openly claims strikes far from its borders, which raises the stakes in a war Russia is fighting with daily attacks on Ukrainian cities.

more: The harbour is nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow. The attack follows a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin called an act of terrorism. Ukraine's long-range drones have also hit Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga, and others have reached deep inside Siberia.

Zelensky calls such strikes "long-range sanctions". The best known was last year's Operation Spider's Web, when a specially adapted lorry released a swarm of explosive drones near a Russian strategic bomber base. The BBC's analysis says the war was already spreading beyond Ukraine's borders before Benghazi.

stories.headline: Pope Francis saw the devil three times and once the "gates of hell", his private diary reveals
stories.short: The late Pope Francis saw the devil three times and once saw the "gates of hell", according to excerpts from his personal diary published on Tuesday in a new book. The Private Diary of Pope Francis, by the Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernández, draws on a black plastic journal Jorge Bergoglio kept from 1992 to 2024.

why.text: It is a rare look inside the private faith and doubts of a pope who was known for speaking plainly in public.

more: The journal reveals his worries, regrets and self-criticism as well as his faith, The Hindu reports. Cardinal Fernández, who heads the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, said Francis had asked him to help make its contents known to the world.

After Francis died last year, Fernández told his successor, Leo XIV, that he feared the journal would be "left forgotten in some storage". He was allowed to publish passages, saying the spiritual concerns in Francis's heart "are very clear and can do us good". One of the most striking passages dates from his years as Archbishop of Buenos Aires.

stories.headline: Bets against Nvidia collapse as its shares rebound on Huang's return, with one leveraged fund losing 92% in a day
stories.short: Nvidia's rebound after its board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday turned bets against the chipmaker into heavy losses. GraniteShares' 2x Short NVDA fund, worth about $100 million, plunged 63%, and in Europe its 3x Short Nvidia product sank 92%. Anthropic's shares also turned positive, climbing to $90.45, nearly 9% above their IPO price.

why.text: Last week's AI sell-off was the worst since 2020, and Monday showed how fast the mood can flip.

more: The GraniteShares fund had been up 46% this year through Friday, riding the sell-off. A Leverage Shares product lost 80%. Leveraged single-stock funds reset their exposure daily, so they magnify every turn in sentiment. This year's sharp swings in AI stocks have handed traders spectacular gains and losses, and the products have turned the biggest technology names into vehicles for aggressive speculation, Bloomberg reports.

Anthropic had lagged the rally before reversing earlier losses. "Nvidia was always more important than Anthropic," said Michael O'Rourke of JonesTrading, noting that Nvidia was once worth $5 trillion. Anthropic's committed spending nears $901 billion through 2045, its filings show, making its early trading a referendum on the sector.

stories.headline: Record foreign buying of ₹1.27 trillion has lifted the Sensex nearly 11% in November despite Monday's fall
stories.short: The Sensex rose 7,976 points, or 10.71%, in November up to Monday, adding ₹34.61 trillion to the value of BSE-listed companies, which now stands at $5.48 trillion. Foreign investors put in a net ₹1.27 trillion this month, the highest monthly inflow ever, after two months in which foreign funds were net sellers.

why.text: India has been the best-performing large market in the world this month, even as the AI rout hit Wall Street.

more: Lower crude prices and better-than-expected September-quarter earnings also helped, along with a stronger rupee. "The dramatic change in the FII stance towards India, rupee appreciation and better-than-expected impressive earnings growth have combined to boost market sentiments," said V K Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments.

Five heavyweights, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Reliance, Airtel and SBI, drove 45% of the Nifty's rise. On Monday the Sensex closed 1.8% lower at 82,436 as banks fell, and Brent crude settled at about $86, its lowest close in three months. Foreign investors had pulled ₹34,843 crore out in October and ₹35,861 crore in September, according to NSDL data.

stories.headline: Brentford beat 10-man Everton 4-0 as James Tarkowski is sent off for the first time in 351 Premier League games
stories.short: Brentford thrashed Everton 4-0 on Monday night, with Keane Lewis-Potter scoring twice and Vitaly Janelt adding a stunner. Everton captain James Tarkowski, who had collected 74 Premier League yellow cards without ever being sent off, was shown his first red, upgraded from a yellow after a VAR review of his challenge on Yehor Yarmoliuk.

why.text: It spoilt David Moyes's record night and leaves Everton without their captain for Sunday's Merseyside derby.

more: It was Moyes's 593rd game as Everton manager, more than anyone in the club's history, and the heaviest defeat since he returned at the start of last year. Tarkowski won the ball but followed through forcefully; referee Craig Pawson first gave a yellow before changing it after watching the replay.

Opinion was split on the decision, and even Moyes was unsure. "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot is high," he told Match of the Day. "Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that."
